questions.question: 1. What is the key characteristic of 'frequency selective fading'?

answers.a: All frequency components of the signal fade in the exact same way.
answers.b: Different frequency components of the signal experience different amounts of fading.
answers.c: The signal's amplitude increases uniformly across all frequencies.
answers.d: The fading only affects the phase, not the amplitude, of the signal.

questions.question: 2. What does 'delay spread' measure in a wireless channel?

answers.a: The time it takes for a signal to leave the transmitter.
answers.b: The difference in arrival time between the first and last multipath components.
answers.c: The speed at which the receiver is moving.
answers.d: The total time duration of a single data bit.

questions.question: 3. Frequency selective fading occurs when the signal's bandwidth is...

answers.a: smaller than the channel's coherence bandwidth.
answers.b: larger than the channel's coherence bandwidth.
answers.c: exactly equal to the channel's coherence bandwidth.
answers.d: not related to the channel's coherence bandwidth.

questions.question: 4. What is the 'coherence bandwidth' of a channel?

answers.a: The total bandwidth allocated to the service provider.
answers.b: The range of frequencies that experience similar or correlated fading.
answers.c: The speed at which the signal frequencies change.
answers.d: The bandwidth that is completely free of any interference.

questions.question: 5. A large delay spread in a channel will result in...
6. What is the primary negative consequence of frequency selective fading?

answers.a: The signal's power becomes too high for the receiver.
answers.b: The signal arrives at the receiver too quickly.
answers.c: It causes intersymbol interference (ISI), where symbols overlap.
answers.d: It causes all frequencies to be lost permanently.

questions.question: 7. If a channel has a very small delay spread (much smaller than the symbol period), what type of fading will the signal likely experience?
8. Intersymbol interference (ISI) is a major problem when...

answers.a: the delay spread is very small compared to the symbol period.
answers.b: the delay spread is large and comparable to or greater than the symbol period.
answers.c: the signal bandwidth is very narrow.

questions.question: 9. How is the coherence bandwidth of a channel related to the delay spread?

answers.c: They are not related in any way.
answers.d: They are equal to each other.

questions.question: 10. A signal is considered to experience flat fading if its bandwidth is...

answers.a: much larger than the coherence bandwidth.
answers.b: much smaller than the coherence bandwidth.
